name: open source
say: Reason four: it's open source — and here that's a promise, not a marketing line. The code is A G P L: free to use, free to study, free to change, and any hosted version has to stay free too. The documentation is Creative Commons. Every module carries a signature, so a fork is verifiable — you can prove exactly what you're running, byte for byte. And if Hypercomb ever goes in a direction you don't like, you can take it in yours, and your hive still opens. That's what open actually has to mean.
